$comment: Registry of BUILT widgets, consumed by the gallery page and scripts/build.mjs. `title` is the gallery card AND the page heading: they used to be allowed to differ, the card naming the topic and the page asking the question, and that split was cut — a student who clicked "Hypothesis Testing" should land on a page that says so. `npm run check` asserts manifest.title === defineWidget({title}) === the index.html <title> prefix; the question belongs in `subtitle`. `blurb` is gallery copy and nothing else reads it. The plan — every candidate concept, its target misconception and evidence — lives in docs/catalogue.md; see that file for why the two are separate. A widget marked shipped there must appear here, and vice versa. NO HEIGHT IS RECORDED HERE, and adding one back needs a reader for it first. It used to live in three files and drift; deleting the embedders (prd §6) left one copy that nothing consumed, and a number nothing reads is a number that drifts silently — by the time it was measured, eight of the nine were 190–310px wrong. Heights are also no longer one number per widget: `bayesian` returns a different one per tab. README's iframe recipe says how to get a correct one.

widgets.title: The Normal Distribution
widgets.blurb: A normal distribution arises when many small independent errors add together.

widgets.title: Central Limit Theorem
widgets.blurb: Sample means become normally distributed, whatever the shape of the population.

widgets.title: Bootstrap Sampling
widgets.blurb: The bootstrap estimates the uncertainty of a sample mean by resampling the sample itself.

widgets.title: Confidence Intervals
widgets.blurb: A confidence interval's level describes how often intervals constructed that way contain the true value.

widgets.title: Hypothesis Testing
widgets.blurb: A permutation test builds the null distribution by shuffling group labels and recomputing the difference.

widgets.title: Multiple Testing
widgets.blurb: Testing thousands of hypotheses inflates false positives; multiple-testing corrections control the error rate.

widgets.title: Decision Making
widgets.blurb: A hypothesis test is a decision whose error rates are set by effect size, sample size and the significance threshold.

widgets.title: Maximum Likelihood
widgets.blurb: Maximum likelihood chooses the parameter values that make the observed data most probable.

widgets.title: Bayesian Estimation
widgets.blurb: Bayesian estimation combines the likelihood with a prior to give a probability distribution over the parameter itself.

widgets.title: Expectation–Maximization
widgets.blurb: Expectation–maximization recovers the component distributions of a mixture without knowing who belongs to which.

widgets.title: Probability Distributions
widgets.blurb: Common distributions, each chosen by the process that generates the measurement.

widgets.title: Odds Ratio and Relative Risk
widgets.blurb: The odds ratio and the relative risk quantify the association between exposure and outcome in a 2×2 table.

widgets.title: Fitting and Generalizing
widgets.blurb: How well a model fits the data it was trained on, and how well it generalizes to data it has never seen.

widgets.title: Linear Models and Regularization
widgets.blurb: A linear model is a weighted sum of features; regularization shrinks the weights to reduce overfitting.

widgets.title: Logistic Regression
widgets.blurb: Logistic regression predicts a binary outcome by modelling the log(odds), so each coefficient is an odds ratio.

widgets.title: Support Vector Machines
widgets.blurb: An SVM finds the maximum-margin boundary between two classes; the kernel determines the shape it can take.

widgets.title: Trees and Ensembles
widgets.blurb: Decision trees split data one threshold at a time; ensembles combine many trees to stabilise the fit.

widgets.title: Balancing Data
widgets.blurb: Class imbalance biases a model toward the majority; rebalancing the data or reweighting the fit corrects it.

widgets.title: Principal Component Analysis
widgets.blurb: Principal component analysis finds the directions of greatest variance and projects the data onto them.

widgets.title: Multidimensional Scaling
widgets.blurb: Multidimensional scaling arranges samples so their distances match a measured distance table as closely as possible.

widgets.title: t-SNE
widgets.blurb: t-SNE embeds high-dimensional data in 2-D, preserving each sample's nearest neighbours rather than global distances.

widgets.title: UMAP
widgets.blurb: UMAP embeds high-dimensional data in 2-D by building a nearest-neighbour graph and laying it out.

widgets.title: K-Means
widgets.blurb: K-means partitions data into K clusters, where the number of clusters must be chosen in advance.

widgets.title: DBSCAN
widgets.blurb: DBSCAN finds clusters as dense regions without choosing their number in advance.

widgets.title: Missing Data
widgets.blurb: The mechanism of missingness (MCAR, MAR or MNAR) determines its bias and whether it can be detected.

widgets.title: Causal Structures
widgets.blurb: The causal structure — fork, pipe or collider — decides whether adjusting for a covariate removes a bias or creates one.

widgets.title: Fitting a Linear Model
widgets.blurb: Fitting a linear model means choosing the intercept and slope that make the sum of squared differences smallest.

widgets.title: Fitting Multiple Covariates
widgets.blurb: Adding a covariate to a linear model changes the other coefficients: each is the effect with the rest held constant.

widgets.title: Fitting a Categorical Covariate
widgets.blurb: A categorical covariate fits group means: each coefficient is the difference from a reference level you choose.

widgets.title: Fitting an Interaction
widgets.blurb: An interaction lets one covariate's effect depend on another, so a main effect is read at the other's zero.

widgets.title: Modeling Time-to-Event Data
widgets.blurb: The Kaplan-Meier estimate keeps censored patients in the risk set until they leave, using everything that was seen.

widgets.title: Modeling Hierarchical Data
widgets.blurb: A linear mixed model counts evidence in patients rather than rows, where repeated measurements are correlated.

widgets.title: Checking the Model Fit
widgets.blurb: Residual diagnostic plots and R² assess how well a linear model fits the data.

widgets.title: Scoring a Classifier
widgets.blurb: The ROC curve traces true and false positive rates across every threshold, and AUC summarises them in one number.

widgets.title: Scoring the Predictions
widgets.blurb: Error metrics score a numeric outcome; the confusion matrix and the ROC curve score a categorical one.

widgets.title: Naive Bayes
widgets.blurb: Naive Bayes classifies by multiplying the prior with one likelihood per feature, treating the features as independent.

widgets.title: Neural Networks (MLP)
widgets.blurb: A multi-layer perceptron composes artificial neurons, and backpropagation adjusts their weights to reduce the loss.

widgets.title: Explaining a Prediction
widgets.blurb: A prediction is divided among its features by averaging what each one adds over every order of arrival.

widgets.title: Normalization and Transformation
widgets.blurb: Normalization corrects technical variation between samples; transformation stabilises variance that grows with size.

widgets.title: Batch Effects
widgets.blurb: The same samples with and without the batch shift, then what each correction method does to the answer.

widgets.title: Matrix Factorization
widgets.blurb: Both NMF and PCA split one matrix into two smaller ones; only one of them is allowed a minus sign.

widgets.title: Hierarchical Clustering
widgets.blurb: Hierarchical clustering builds a dendrogram from the distances between observations, then cuts it into k clusters.

widgets.title: Enrichment Analysis
widgets.blurb: Overrepresentation uses threshold-based gene selection; the enrichment score ranks the entire expression profile.
